claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship the upgrade path with the component itself.
A Pulumi component state migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Pulumi component state migrations are a new feature.
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
A component state migrations discussion exists at github.com/pulumi/pulumi/discussions/24799.
The v1 example uses the legacy `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc` component, creating a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and its association, and an internet gateway.
Replacing an AWS VPC requires replacing a security group that refers to the VPC's ID (per the AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId documentation).
A replacement database does not automatically contain the old database's data.
The modern AWSX component is `awsx.ec2.Vpc`.
The third version of the example removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.
Each record in Pulumi state has a Pulumi name called a URN, and managed resources also have an ID from the cloud provider.
The legacy AWSX component wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components, while modern AWSX removes those wrappers.
In the example, the Pulumi name of the subnet changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1`.
Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when its saved state remains compatible.
Pulumi resource registration accepts a `stateMigrations` option taking a migration callback, alongside an alias for the legacy component type.
The alias lets Pulumi find the old component, and the migration callback receives the component's saved state followed by the state of its children.

The state migration callback returns `newState` (the complete set of records replacing the old component and its children) and `successors` (a map from each disappearing old URN to the URN that replaces it).
In the example migration, an unexpected component type raises an error, and the callback does nothing if state already uses modern AWSX or plain AWS resources.
The example's `rename` helper copies the saved record, changes its URN, type, and parent, and preserves the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.
Pulumi uses the `successors` mappings to update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack.
The second migration removes the AWSX VPC component record and moves the managed VPC into its place, and the VPC keeps its AWS ID.
Pulumi runs state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next callback.
A stack still using legacy AWSX can upgrade directly to the plain AWS version, and a stack already on modern AWSX skips the first migration.

After a state migration, Pulumi compares the new program with the migrated state and calls the provider for remaining changes; the example can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
Running `pulumi preview` evaluates the migration without saving it, and the update (`pulumi up`) saves the migrated state.

When users upgrade a component that registers a state migration and run Pulumi, it runs the migration as part of the normal preview and update without users writing the migration or attaching the callback.
The component state migrations guide covers the callback contract, and the VPC example contains all three programs and the migration code.
Pulumi state migration callbacks (the stateMigrations resource option) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
Pulumi state migration callbacks must be idempotent and return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
Pulumi state migration callbacks rewrite state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a component state migration callback returns no result.

The state entries passed to a component state migration callback use the Pulumi checkpoint resource format, including fields such as `urn`, `type`, `id`, `parent`, `provider`, `inputs`, and `outputs`.
The stateMigrations resource option reference page documents the callback API at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/#callback-api.
A component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
The restrictions on state-changing migration results (for update plans or targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied migration.
